description.narrative: The development objective of the Scaling-up Participatory Sustainable Forest Management Project for Lao People's Democratic Republic is to execute Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation (REDD+) activities through participatory sustainable forest management in priority areas and to pilot forest landscape management in four provinces. The project has four components. The first component is strengthening and expanding Participatory Sustainable Forest Management (PSFM) in production forest areas. It has following two sub-components: (1) developing partnerships to increase implementation capacity. This subcomponent will support development of strategic partnerships and collaborative arrangements with national institutions and Non-Profit Associations (NPAs). Regional and international agencies will also be contracted to augment strategic skills as needed; and (2) community engagement in PSFM and village livelihood development. This subcomponent will finance village livelihood grants to implement Community Action Plans (CAPs) and finance the review, and revision of key social, institutional and technical guidelines for implementation of PSFM and Village Livelihood Development (VLD). The second component is piloting forest landscape management. It has following two sub-components: (a) developing methodologies and frameworks for forest landscape management. This sub component will support the development and adoption of a landscape approach for forest and biodiversity resources management in four Northern provinces in Lao People's Democratic Republic (PDR).; and (b) establishing forest landscape pilots. Under this sub-component support will be provided for designing provincial pilots based on the mechanisms and frameworks developed under subcomponent 2a. The third component is enabling legal and regulatory environment. This component has following three sub-components: (i) strengthening legal and regulatory frameworks. This sub-component will support development of legal and regulatory frameworks for implementation of PSFM and frameworks for Forest Landscape Management (FLM); (ii) strengthening forest law enforcement and governance. This sub-component will strengthen forest law enforcement and governance through Department of Forest Inspection (DoFI) implementation of the national forest law enforcement strategy 2020; and (iii) creating public awareness for climate change and REDD+. This sub-component will support Government of Lao PDR (GoL) efforts to create public awareness for climate change and REDD+ by designing a national communication strategy and a public awareness campaign. The fourth component is project management. This component will cover project management at the national and sub-national level, Technical Assistance (TA), and monitoring and evaluation.
To strengthen participatory sustainable forest management in targeted production forest areas, and forest landscape management in targeted provinces

The Recipient shall maintain throughout implementation of theProject with a mandate, terms of reference, composition and resources satisfactory to the Association: (a) a National ProjectSteering Committee chaired by the Vice-Minister of MAF, to provide policy guidance and enhance inter-ministerial coordination andwith representation from, inter alia: (i) ministries including MAF, MoNRE, MOF, MPI, MoIC; (ii) DAEC and NAFRI; (iii) LFND and LWU;and (iv) PPSC and DPSC; (b) a NPMO which shall be responsible for, inter alia: overall project coordination and management, at thenational and province level including financial management, procurement, monitoring and reporting; implementation of nationallevel Project components related to policy, legal issues, and forest sector monitoring; the NPMO shall have a national Projectmanager, and adequate finance and procurement staff; (c) a PPMO in each province with the PAFO chief as the provincial Projectmanager; the PPMO shall be responsible for, inter alia, the management and implementation of Project work plans, organizingcapacity building activities, financial arrangements, coordination, and monitoring;(d) a DPMO in each Project District with theDAFO chief as the District Project manager; the DPMO shall be responsible for, inter alia, the management and implementation ofProject work plans at the grassroot level, coordinating field staff, and NPAs and LFND and LWU; and (e) a PPSC and DPSC in eachprovince and Project District chaired by the provincial vice governor, and district governor respectively, with membership from,inter alia, local level departments and divisions.

In carrying out the Project, the Recipient, through MAF, shall maintain in eachPAFO of each participating province a financial management system satisfactory to the Association.

title.narrative: VLD Grants disbursed to villages and under implementation
Areas with Forest Landscape Management implementation plans

comment.narrative:
<p>In the 2018 restructuring, the wording was changed to be more general to better accommodate the current framework for FLM in LaoPDR. The Forest Landscape Management area comprises areas managed by several entities and some of them may not have annual plans, but more general long-term plans combined with short-term operational plans.</p>

<p>In the 2020 restructuring, the target was achieved and surpassed. Therefore the target was increased to match the actual value from the May 2019 ISR. The AF aimed to maintain this achievement.</p>

<p>At project completion in 2022, the indicator is fully achieved.</p>

title.narrative: Areas with Forest Landscape Management implementation plans
Reduced emissions from deforestation and forest degradation (tCO2e)

comment.narrative:
<p>In the 2018 restructuring, </p>

<p>The qualifier “selected PSFM areas” was dropped in view of forest law enforcement activities undertaken by the project for the entire country as opposed to selected PSFM areas only. The carbon quantificationmethodology was also redefined: 1) deforestation was taken out of consideration due to methodological complexity; and 2) only reduced forest degradation due to reduced illegal logging was considered with the assumption that project-supported law enforcement helped reduce illegal logging.</p>

<p>In the 2020 restructuring, the target was raised to 2,000,000. The original target was achieved and surpassed, and the new target was based on the actual value from May 2019 ISR - 1,800,000. The AF aimed to further increase the end target to 2,000,000.</p>

<p>At project completion, the revised target was only 90% achieved. </p>

title.narrative: Reduced emissions from deforestation and forest degradation (tCO2e)
Enhanced carbon storage from improved forest protection and restoration (tCO2e)
Forest area brought under forest landscape management plans

comment.narrative:
<p>In the 2018 restructuring, the definition was adjusted to add clarity and to align with the government’s approach to “Re-delineation of 3 Forest Categories” which essentially aimed to define the future forest area (i.e., current area under the 3 forest categories and area of “good” forests outside of them). The FLM area has been defined through remote sensing, field checks and consultations with stakeholders.</p>

<p>In the 2020 restructuring, the original target was achieved and surpassed. Therefore the target was increased to match the actual value from the May 2019 ISR. The AF aimed to maintain this achievement.</p>

<p>At project completion in 2022 the target was fully achieved.</p>

title.narrative: Forest area brought under forest landscape management plans

comment.narrative:
<p>In the 2018 restructuring the wording and unit of measurement were revised. The wording "under the project that are assessed as complete” was dropped because cross-sectoral development cannot be sufficiently completed by a single project or sector. After looking into several options, the responsibility for implementing FLM frameworks was assigned to provincial REDD+ Task Forces which have a cross-sectoral outreach due to the nature of REDD+.</p>
<p>At project completion in 2022 the target was fully achieved.</p>

title.narrative: Beneficiaries who receive technical services of adequate quality

comment.narrative:
<p>In the 2018 restructuring the indicator wording was modified with the word 'percentage' dropped. </p>

<p>In the 2020 restructuring, the target was raised to 83%, assuming that the 80% original target was achieved and willing to slightly increase it during the AF. </p>

<p>By project closure in 2022, the indicator was 91% achieved.</p>

title.narrative: Participants who perceive the CEF process is adequate

comment.narrative:
<p>In the 2018 restructuring, the indicator wording was slightly modified for precision, maintaining the relevance and target of the indicator.</p>

<p>In the 2020 restructuring, the original target was achieved and surpassed. Therefore, the target was increased to 97 to matches the actual value from the May 2019 ISR. The AF aimed to maintain this achievement.</p>

<p>At project completion in 2022, the target was fully achieved. </p>

Rate of annual forest cover loss in targeted Production Forest Areas
Rate of annual forest cover loss in targeted Production Forest Areas

comment.narrative:
<p>In the 2018 restructuring, the indicator was adjusted because the methodology used for quantifying the baseline at appraisal wasnot documented; the original indicator was thus deemed no longer appropriate for measuring the outcome. The baseline was reset at 0.27, based on the average annual forest loss rate from 2010-2015 estimated by the project-supported PFA forest cover change assessment study in 2016. The target was also adjusted to be consistent with PDO Indicators 5 and 6, from 0.15 to 0.18. The wording was slightly changed too. </p>

<p>In the 2020 restructuring, the target was achieved and surpassed. Thus the target was increased to match the actual value from May 2019 ISR, and the AF aimed to maintain this achievement.</p>

<p>At project completion, the target was fully achieved. </p>

<p>In the 2018 restructuring the indicator wording, baseline, measurement unit, and target were substantially revised. The originalindicator explicitly mentioned strengthened tenure, without fully defining indices or measures. The MoU is the instrument selected by the government to strengthen tenure in PFAs and is easily quantifiable. The baseline has been set at zero and the target hasbeen reduced to account for the inaccessibility of some areas for security reasons at 975,000 ha (see PDO 1). Finally the measurement unit was changed from square km to ha. </p>

<p>In the 2020 restructuring, the target was achieved and surpassed. Therefore,the target was increased to 976,211 to match the actual value from the May 2019 ISR. The AF aimed to maintain this achievement.</p>

<p>At project completion, the target was fully achieved.</p>

title.narrative: Forest area brought under management plans

comment.narrative:
<p>In the 2018 restructuring, the baseline was reduced to zero to exclude the area for which management plans had already been prepared prior to SUPSFM. The target was also adjusted to 975,000 to take into consideration the area that was inaccessible for security reasons in Xaysomboun Province.</p>

<p>In the 2020 restructuring, the target was raised from 975,000 to 976,000. The increase matches the actual value from May 2019 ISR with the aim for the AF to maintain this achievement.</p>

<p>At project closing in 2022, the target was achieved and slightly surpassed. The total area under PSFM plans has been determined by summing up the aras provided in the 40 individual PSFM plans prepared with support from SU-PSFM.</p>

title.narrative: Enhanced carbon storage from improved forest protection and restoration (tCO2e)

comment.narrative:
<p>In the 2018 the baseline was revised to zero. The indicator wording was also modified: the qualifier “in selected PSFM” was dropped in view of that fact that some of the agroforestry sub-projects intended to enhance carbon storage were undertaken outside the PFAs. The carbon quantification methodology was also redefined: average carbon sequestration potential of agroforestry subprojects (determined as 2,500 tonnes/month) multiplied by the number of relevant subprojects. The target remained the same. </p>

<p>In the 2020 restructuring, the target was raised to 35,000 to reflect actual results in 2019 - 33,000, which surpassed the original target.</p>

<p>At project completion the target was not fully achieved. </p>

<p>Calculations were based on the following assumptions:</p>

<ul>
 <li>average monthly sequestration if all village projects successfully implemented: 2,500 tCO2e;</li>
 <li>Since May 2018, 100 % of village projects were under implementation (48 months); based on evaluation on the AF village projects, the success rate is assumed to be same, 90%.</li>
</ul>

title.narrative: People in forest and adjacent community with monetary/ non-monetary benefit from interventions

comment.narrative:
<p>Originally included as a corporate “Core Sector Indicator” (CSI).</p>

<p>In the 2018 restructuring, with the discontinuation of the CSIs, the wording was adjusted to better capture the benefits derived from the relevant project interventions. The definition of the indicator was also adjusted to include only direct beneficiaries of the VLDGs as opposed to populations benefiting from forests more broadly. The baseline was set to zero thus reflecting into the adjustment of the target to 115,000 (which remains unchanged in absolute value).</p>

<p>In the 2020 restructuring the target was achieved and surpassed. The increase to 117,400 matches the actual value from May 2019 ISR which the AF aimed to maintain.</p>

<p>At project completion in 2022 the target was achieved.</p>

title.narrative: Aggregate forest area under certification as a result of the project

comment.narrative:
<p>In the 2018 restructuring, the indicator wording, target and measurement unit were revised. The word “as a result of the project” was added to the definition to make the indicator more specific. The indicator unit was changed from square km to ha to allow easier comparability of different efforts. Baseline was set to zero to reflect that actual situation of PSFM. The end target was reduced to 175,000 ha because the forest area suitable for commercial wood production is smaller than the estimate made at the time of preparing the project when full information was not available.</p>

<p>In the 2020 restructuring the end target was increased to match the renewed national target set by the Government at 230,000 ha by 2022. </p>

<p>At project completion in 2022, the indicator was 43% achieved. Part of the reason is the Covid-19 travel restrictions, which delayed andlimited the auditors 2020 and 2021 certification missions. More structurally, the continued extension of the logging ban resulted in reluctance to bear certification costs for a resource without realizing any financial benefits. </p>

<p> </p>

title.narrative: VLD Grants disbursed to villages and under implementation

comment.narrative:
<p>In the 2018 restructuring the indicator wording was revised to better reflect the activities directly financed and delivered by the project. The old indicator was 'Percentage of CAPs and Village Development Plans under implementation'. The main activity is the preparation and implementation of VLD grants. The new indicator reflects the fact that Community Action Plans (CAP) are a broad village planning framework (only selected activities under CAPs are implemented using funds from VLD Grants), and Village Development Plans are not developed under the project but are part of broader local governance. The SUFORD-SU Project has supported the formulation of CAPs and finances priority community-selected activities within them. The target remains relevant.</p>

<p>In the 2020 restructuring the target was already achieved. </p>

<p>At project completion in 2022, the target was fully achieved.</p>

title.narrative: Reforms in forest policy, legislation or other regulations supported

comment.narrative:
<p>The project exceeded the expectations under the original formulation of the indicator, as the project was instrumental to the deep reform that the forestry sector underwent in the 9 years of implementation.</p>
<p>Support has been provided to completed or ongoing policy or legal work on village forestry, salvage logging, preparation of the pending new Forest Law (including forestry legal compendium, wildlife and aquatic legal compendium, penal code, TLAS, Forest Certification Systems), implementation ofPMO-15, National REDD+ Strategy, approval of PMO5 (wildlife law enforcement), and PMO9 allowing forest plantation in PFAs.</p>

title.narrative: Reforms in forest policy, legislation or other regulations supported
POFIs in compliance with DOFI best management practice operating procedures
STEPP field activities resulting in enforcement action
Investigations of breaches of forestry law and wildlife and aquatic law referred to criminal courts

comment.narrative:
<p>In the 2018 restructuring, the wording, baseline and target were revised. The wording "successfully concluded" was dropped and replaced. The original indicator did not capture the salient points of investigative activity. It referred only to Forestry Law and excludes Wildlife and Aquatic Law which is a critical area of enforcement. Also, it did not distinguish between the types of investigative "conclusions". Administrative procedures are considerably easier to "conclude" than cases referred to criminal courts. Accordingly, the indicator scope was been broadened to cover activities related to Wildlife and Aquatic Law. At the same time, it was given a sharper focus by limiting it to cases that reach criminal courts. The outcome of the court cases is left out of the indicator scope as the project was not directly involved and could not contribute to the otcome. The baseline was set at zero to capture only the project contributions, and the target was reduced to 5 percent as the nature of the cases monitored changed.</p>

<p>The original target of 5 was achieved and surpassed. Based on the highly satisfactory performance of this activity, the target was doubled to 10 percent for the 2020 restructuring and AF, also considering the inceased inter-agency coordination envisaged under AF that would likely increase the number of successful investigations.</p>

<p>Of the 5,655 investigations carried out over the total project funding period (Oct 2013-May 2022), about 7.5 percent (425) have been referred to criminal courts. </p>

<p>During the AF funding period (2020-May 2022 DOFI undertook 19 joint investigations with the Environmental Police and 1 with the Army, all of which were referred to criminal courts. This was 14% of all referrals (142) duing this period. </p>

<p>Challenges have been identified in the lack of a clear operational pathway for meaningful joint investigations among DOFI, Environmental Police, and Customs. </p>

<p>At the provincial level, the groundwork for achieving strengthened interagency law enforcement cooperation has been achieved by DOFI in Khammouane and Bolikhamxay provinces, through the development of pilot operational guidelines for Provincial Wildlife Enforcement Networks (P-WEN), but further work on the pilots is needed to get to official approval.?????</p>

<p>??</p>

<p>In the 2018 restructuring the indicator wording, baseline, measurement unit, and target were substantially revised. The originalindicator explicitly mentioned strengthened tenure, and aimed to measure community land titles issued. In the absence of a legislation for issuing land titles inside state forestland, The MoU or the Village Forest Management Agreement (VFMA) is the instrument selected by the government to strengthen tenure in village forests. The target was set at 10,000ha. The measurement unitwas revised from absolute numbers of titles to ha of forest under MoU. </p>

<p>In the 2020 restructuring, the target was achieved and surpassed. Therefore target was increased to match the actual value from May 2019 ISR - 10,750. The AF aimed to maintain this achievement.</p>

<p>At project completion in 2022, the target was fully achieved.</p>

title.narrative: POFIs in compliance with DOFI best management practice operating procedures

comment.narrative:
<p>The indicator was introduced in the 2018 restructuring.</p>
<p>18 of the 18 provinces have an average score between 1 and 3 (on a 5-point scale) in monthly evaluation audits of their compliance in 8 areas of work: (a) patrol activity, (b) timber seizures, (c) wildlife seizures, (d) NTFP, (e) land illegally cleared, (f) equipment, (g) investigations, and (h) community education activity). An average score of 4 or 5 indicates failure to pass the audits. Figure based on DOFI internal evaluation report finalized in April 2022.</p>

title.narrative: STEPP field activities resulting in enforcement action

comment.narrative:
<p>The indicator was introduced in the 2018 restructuring. Under SUPSFM the main tool for enforcement is STEPP (the Strategic and Tactical Enforcement Patrol Program) which is implemented through systematic patrolling. To indicate whether the proposed shift from education (informal settlement) towards enforcement is taking place, the indicator measures the proportion of human resources dedicated to patrolling as opposed to education and administration.</p>

<p>In the 2020 restructuring, the target was achieved and surpassed. The target was increased from 80 to 85 percent to match the actual value from May 2019 ISR. The AF aimed to maintain this achievement.</p>

<p>At project completion in 2022, the target was achieved at 96 percent. </p>

<p>The figure refers to total investigations minus ongoing:</p>

<ul>
 <li>2017 (baseline): 710 cases-152 = 558 (79%). </li>
 <li>2021 = Actual (Current): 699 cases-124 = 82.2% (2021 is the last full year).</li>
</ul>

<p>This is a new indicator approved in the 2020 AF to address the absence of provincial investment plans to sequence and locate public and private projects within a landscape of different forest and land uses. The investment plans, currently under development but delayed by restrictions related to Covid-19, will highlight tradeoffs among land uses within the landscape, to help reduce risks to investment. </p>
<p>While considerable progress was made and key data collected, the output was not yet sufficient to finalize and roll-out approved plans before project closing. However, the overall outcome of the project will not be significantly affected, as the FLIPs were designed to strengthen and enhance the sustainability of project outcomes that were already mostly achieved. Finalization and approval of the FLIPs will be undertaken by the closely related Landscapes and Livelihoods project (P170559) under which the plans are intended to provide continuing support to decision making at landscape level.</p>
